raw_text:
Below is a complete 12-week muscle-gain program tailored for your new client: a 26-year-old female, strict vegan, recreational lifter, full-gym access. The plan includes periodization (three 4-week phases), detailed weekly sessions, exercise selection, sets/reps, progression guidelines, deloads, and a plant-based nutrition strategy to reach ~150 g protein/day plus recovery notes and sample meal suggestions. Assume she has no injuries; adjust if any mobility or medical issues arise.

Overview and goals
- Primary goal: hypertrophy (muscle gain) over 12 weeks.
- Secondary goals: strength increases, improved movement quality.
- Training frequency: 4 gym sessions per week (push/pull/legs/full or upper/lower split with hypertrophy focus); optional light conditioning and mobility.
- Progression model: linear progression across each 4-week block (week 1–3 increase intensity or reps; week 4 is a lighter “deload/auto-regulation” week).
- Load guidance: for primary lifts use 6–12 RM ranges for hypertrophy; use 60–80%+ of 1RM as appropriate. Track loads and increase 2.5–5% when target reps are hit for all sets.
- Time per session: 60–75 minutes.

Phase structure
- Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Foundations — build volume tolerance, technique, moderate loads. Emphasis on compound lifts, 8–12 rep ranges.
- Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Volume + intensity — increase load and slightly lower rep ranges for main lifts (6–10), increase accessory volume for hypertrophy.
- Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Peak hypertrophy & strength carryover — heavier intensity on main lifts (5–8) with continued high accessory volume, final deload in week 12.

Weekly layout (consistent across phases, with exercise, sets/reps noted for each week and progression rules)
- Day 1: Upper (Push emphasis)
- Day 2: Lower (Quad-dominant)
- Day 3: Rest or active recovery (mobility, low-intensity cardio)
- Day 4: Upper (Pull emphasis)
- Day 5: Lower (Hip-dominant / posterior chain)
- Day 6: Full-body accessory / weak-point work + optional conditioning
- Day 7: Rest

Detailed week-by-week program

Phase 1 — Weeks 1–4: Foundations (higher reps, establish baseline)
Progression rule: Weeks 1→3 increase load slightly if you can complete prescribed reps on all work sets; Week 4 is a lighter week (reduce sets by ~20% or reduce load by 5–10% and reduce RPE).

Week 1
Day 1 — Upper (Push focus)
- Barbell bench press (or dumbbell variant): 4 sets × 8–10 reps
- Overhead dumbbell press: 3 × 10–12
- Incline dumbbell press (moderate incline): 3 × 10–12
- Cable lateral raises: 3 × 12–15
- Triceps rope pushdown: 3 × 12–15
- Core: Plank 3 × 45–60s

Day 2 — Lower (Quad focus)
- Back squat (or front if mobility limited): 4 × 8–10
- Bulgarian split squat (bodyweight or dumbbell): 3 × 10 each leg
- Leg press: 3 × 12
- Romanian deadlift (light-moderate): 3 × 10–12
- Standing calf raise: 4 × 12–15
- Core: Hanging leg raise 3 × 10–12

Day 4 — Upper (Pull focus)
- Barbell row (or chest-supported row): 4 × 8–10
- Pull-ups or assisted pull-ups / lat pulldown: 4 × 8–10
- Seated cable row (neutral grip): 3 × 10–12
- Face pulls: 3 × 12–15
- Dumbbell hammer curls: 3 × 10–12
- Rear delt fly (machine or dumbbell): 3 × 12–15

Day 5 — Lower (Hip / posterior chain)
- Deadlift (conventional or trap bar): 4 × 6–8 (moderate weight, focus on form)
- Hip thrusts (bell or barbell): 4 × 8–10
- Good mornings or single-leg Romanian deadlift: 3 × 10 each leg
- Glute-ham raise or Nordic curl (assisted if needed): 3 × 8–10
- Seated calf raise: 4 × 12–15
- Core: Deadbug 3 × 10 each side

Day 6 — Full-body accessory + conditioning
- Incline dumbbell bench: 3 × 10–12 (light)
- Goblet squat: 3 × 12–15
- Single-arm dumbbell row: 3 × 10 each side
- Farmer carries 3 × 40–60 m
- Optional conditioning: 12–20 min low-impact interval bike or row

Week 2
- Repeat Week 1. Aim to add small weight increases (2.5–5%) when sets/reps are completed with good technique. Keep rest 60–120s for compounds, 45–75s for accessories.

Week 3
- Repeat Week 1 pattern but try to increase load or 1–2 reps per set if possible. Keep the final set of main lifts at RPE ~8.

Week 4 (deload/style adjustment)
- Reduce total sets by ~20% (e.g., 3→2 on some accessories) or reduce load 5–10%. Keep movement and technique focus. Use this week to address mobility and recovery.

Phase 2 — Weeks 5–8: Build volume and intensity
- Shift rep ranges slightly lower on main lifts to 6–10, increase accessory volume. Continue one lighter week (Week 8) as a recovery/auto-regulation week.

Weeks 5–7 (progressive)
Day 1 — Upper (Push)
- Barbell bench press: 5 × 6–8
- Overhead press (barbell or heavy dumbbell): 4 × 6–8
- Incline dumbbell press: 3 × 8–10
- Dumbbell lateral raise superset with cable front raise: 3 × 12 each
- Weighted dips or machine dips (if possible): 3 × 8–10
- Triceps overhead rope extension: 3 × 10–12

Day 2 — Lower (Quad)
- Squat (back/front variation): 5 × 6–8
- Bulgarian split squat (heavier): 4 × 8 each
- Leg press (heavy): 4 × 8–10
- Romanian deadlift (moderate): 3 × 8–10
- Standing calf raise: 5 × 10–15

Day 4 — Upper (Pull)
- Weighted pull-ups or heavy lat pulldown: 5 × 6–8
- Barbell row (or T-bar): 4 × 6–8
- Single-arm row: 3 × 8–10
- Face pulls: 4 × 12–15
- EZ-bar curls: 3 × 8–10
- Rear delt machine / reverse pec deck: 3 × 12–15

Day 5 — Lower (Posterior)
- Deadlift or trap-bar deadlift: 4 × 5–6 (heavier but controlled)
- Barbell hip thrust: 5 × 6–8 (heavier)
- Walking lunges: 3 × 10–12 steps each leg
- Glute-ham raise or hyperextensions: 3 × 10–12
- Seated calf raise: 4 × 10–15

Day 6 — Full-body accessory / conditioning
- Light compound circuit: 3 rounds (DB incline 10 reps, goblet squat 12, single-arm row 10 each, plank 60s)
- Conditioning: 15–20 minutes moderate-intensity cardio (bike/row)

Week 8 (deload / autoreg)
- Reduce load 10% or reduce sets by 25%. Focus on mobility, foam rolling. Keep one or two lighter technical compound sets.

Phase 3 — Weeks 9–12: Peak hypertrophy + strength carryover
- Emphasis on slightly lower reps on main lifts (5–8) with high accessory volume. Week 12 is a taper/deload with reduced volume so she can evaluate progress.

Weeks 9–11 (progressive)
Day 1 — Upper (Push)
- Bench press: 5 × 5–7 (work up to heavier, final sets at RPE 8–9)
- Overhead press: 4 × 5–7
- Incline dumbbell press: 4 × 8
- Lateral raises (higher volume): 4 × 12–15
- Close-grip bench or weighted dips: 3 × 6–8
- Triceps pushdown drop set: 3 × 10 (then lighter set to failure)

Day 2 — Lower (Quad emphasis)
- Squat or front squat: 5 × 5–7
- Hack squat or leg press: 4 × 8
- Bulgarian split squat (heavy): 4 × 8 each
- Stiff-leg deadlift or single-leg RDL: 3 × 8–10
- Calves: 5 × 10–15

Day 4 — Upper (Pull)
- Weighted pull-ups: 5 × 5–7 (or heavy lat pulldowns)
- Bent-over row / pendlay row: 4 × 6–8
- Chest-supported row: 4 × 8–10
- Face pulls: 4 × 15
- Dumbbell curl superset with hammer curl: 3 × 8–10 each
- Rear delt work: 3 × 12–15

Day 5 — Lower (Posterior)
- Deadlift or trap-bar: 4 × 4–6 (heavier)
- Barbell hip thrust: 5 × 5–7 (heavy)
- Reverse lunges or step-ups: 3 × 8–10 each
- Glute-ham raise / back extensions: 3 × 8–12
- Calf work: 4 × 12–15

Day 6 — Full-body accessory + metabolic
- Compound accessory circuit: 3–4 rounds (KB swings 12, push-up 10–12, DB row 8 each, walking lunge 10 each)
- Conditioning: 10–15 min HIIT or 20 min moderate cardio

Week 12 (taper/deload & testing)
- Reduce overall volume 40% and train at moderate intensities. Use this week to test 3–5RM on main lifts (if comfortable) or take a full recovery week depending on fatigue.

Progression & autoregulation notes
- Aim to add small increments (2.5–5%) once all sets meet top end of rep range for two sessions in a row.
- If unable to meet target reps on >2 sets, keep same load next session or reduce by 2.5–5% as needed.
- Track RPE. Work sets generally RPE 7–9 for hypertrophy phases; RPE 8–9 on heavier weeks.
- Use proper warm-up: 5–10 min cardio, dynamic mobility, 2–3 warm-up sets on compound lifts.

Vegan nutrition plan to hit ~150 g protein/day
Assumptions
- She is aiming for muscle gain: caloric surplus of ~250–500 kcal/day above maintenance is a common target (adjust depending on current body composition and rate of gain desired). I’ll give macro guidance and foods to reach 150 g protein/day.
- Protein target: 150 g/day (plant-only). Spread 4–5 meals + 1–2 protein-rich snacks.
- Aim for 1.6–2.2 g/kg bodyweight if her weight is ~68–94 kg range; you can adjust. If you tell me her bodyweight I’ll set a precise calorie target.

Macro example (example for ~2200–2600 kcal/day; adjust to her needs)
- Protein: 150 g (~600 kcal)
- Fat: 70–90 g (~630–810 kcal)
- Carbs: remaining calories (~260–350 g)

Protein sources and sample daily plan
- Important: use concentrated plant proteins and complete protein pairing, and consider a high-quality vegan protein powder (pea, rice/pea blend, soy if acceptable) to help reach 150 g.
- Suggested protein-rich foods (with approximate protein per common serving):
  - Pea protein isolate powder: 20–30 g protein per scoop
  - Soy protein isolate / TVP / textured soy (if she eats soy): 20–30 g per serving
  - Seitan: 20–25 g per 100 g
  - Tofu (firm): ~15–20 g per 200 g
  - Tempeh: ~19 g per 100 g
  - Lentils (cooked): ~9 g per 100 g (approx 18 g per cup)
  - Chickpeas (cooked): ~8–9 g per 100 g
  - Black beans / kidney beans: ~8 g per 100 g
  - Edamame: ~11 g per 100 g
  - Nuts and seeds: almonds ~6 g / oz; peanut butter ~7–8 g / 2 tbsp; hemp seeds ~9–10 g / 3 tbsp
  - Oats: ~6 g per 40 g (dry)
  - Nutritional yeast: ~8 g per 2 tbsp
  - Plant milk (fortified): ~7–10 g per cup (if protein-fortified varieties)
  - Vegan protein bars (check labels): 15–20 g each

Sample day (approximate protein tallies)
- Breakfast (≈35 g protein)
  - Smoothie: 1.5 scoops pea/rice protein (30 g), 1 cup fortified soy or pea milk (8–10 g), 1/2 cup oats (3–4 g), handful spinach (1–2 g) → adjust to total ~35–40 g
- Snack (≈15–20 g)
  - 1 serving edamame (150 g cooked) ~15–18 g
- Lunch (≈35–40 g)
  - Tempeh bowl: 150–200 g tempeh (~30–40 g) + quinoa (1 cup cooked ~8 g) and veggies → aiming ~35–45 g
- Pre-work snack (≈10–15 g)
  - 1 scoop protein or 2 tbsp peanut butter + banana on rice cakes → ~10–15 g
- Post-work / dinner (≈30–35 g)
  - Seitan stir-fry or tofu/legume combo: 150–200 g seitan (~30–40 g) OR 200 g firm tofu (~20–24 g) + 1 cup lentils (~18 g) split servings → adjust to ~30–35 g
- Evening snack (≈10 g)
  - Dairy-free yogurt with 2 tbsp hemp seeds (~8–10 g) or protein pudding with plant protein

Total: ~150 g protein (use a protein powder scoop to top up if necessary).

Practical protein examples and combinations
- Breakfast smoothie with 1.5–2 scoops vegan protein, oats, milk = 35–45 g.
- Lunch tempeh (200 g) + quinoa = ~40–45 g.
- Dinner seitan (150 g) + beans/veg = ~35–40 g.
- Snacks: edamame, protein bars, hummus + whole grain pita, peanut butter, hemp seeds, nutritional yeast sprinkled on dishes.

Supplement recommendations (vegan-safe)
- High-quality vegan protein powder (pea/rice blend or soy isolate) — convenient for daily hitting of 150 g.
- Creatine monohydrate 3–5 g/day (vegan, supports strength/hypertrophy).
- Vitamin B12 supplement (essential).
- Vitamin D if low sun exposure (D3 vegan algae source).
- Omega-3 (algal DHA/EPA) supplement if desired.
- Consider a multivitamin with iron if dietary intake low; track iron and zinc status.

Meal timing and distribution
- Spread protein across 3–5 meals (aim 25–40 g per meal) — this is effective for muscle protein synthesis.
- Pre- and post-workout: aim for 20–40 g protein around the workout window; carbohydrates to fuel and refill glycogen (30–60 g carbs around workout).
- Night: a protein-containing snack can help total daily intake.

Recovery, sleep, and other lifestyle
- Sleep: target 7–9 hours per night for optimal recovery.
- Hydration: 2–3 L daily (more with heavy sweat).
- Active recovery: mobility work and foam rolling 2–3 times/week, light walks on rest days.
- Monitor fatigue and adjust energy intake upward if she’s losing weight or strength too fast; reduce if gaining too quickly (>0.8–1.0% bodyweight/week).

Tracking and testing
- Track workouts (weights, sets, reps) and protein intake daily (apps or food log).
- Reassess body composition/measurements and strength at the end of each 4-week block. Use week 12 to test 3–5RM or measure progress in photos and measurements.
- Adjust calories by ±200 kcal depending on rate of gain and desired body composition.

Sample grocery list (protein-focused vegan)
- Pea/rice protein powder, seitan, tempeh, tofu, edamame, lentils, chickpeas, black beans, quinoa, oats, hemp seeds, chia seeds, peanut/almond butter, fortified plant milks, nutritional yeast, nuts, whole-grain bread/pasta, potatoes, a variety of vegetables and fruits, olive oil.

Notes on variety and digestibility
- Include diverse plant proteins to ensure a good amino acid profile. Combining cereals (quinoa, rice) and legumes is effective; pea and rice protein powders together create a full amino acid complement.
- Some people find high legume intake causes GI discomfort; adjust fiber intake and spread legumes across meals, and use soaked/cooked properly, canned and rinsed options, or enzyme aids if needed.

Safety and personalization
- If she is new to heavy compound lifts (deadlifts, squats, bench), start with lighter loads and emphasize form; consider one or two technique-focused sessions or working with you directly for technique coaching.
- If she has any medical conditions (e.g., anemia, thyroid), get clearance and tailor macros or supplement needs accordingly.

If you’d like, I can:
- Convert this into a printable week-by-week table or PDF.
- Build a 7-day sample meal plan with exact portion sizes and calories tailored to her current bodyweight and target daily calories.
- Adjust training volume up/down (3 to 5 days/week) depending on her schedule or recovery.

Tell me her bodyweight (and approximate maintenance calories if known) and whether she eats soy and seitan (some vegans avoid gluten), and I’ll produce an exact calorie plan and daily meal-by-meal breakdown to hit 150 g protein.
